en: During a typhoon, stay away from windows because strong winds can shatter the glass and cause severe cuts.
Washing your hands after playing in soil prevents hookworm parasites from entering your body through the skin.
Never taste unknown rocks or minerals because some, like galena, contain toxic lead that can poison you.
Boiling floodwater for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria, making it safe to drink during emergencies.
Looking directly at the sun without certified eclipse glasses can permanently burn your retinas and cause blindness.
Finding the North Star, Polaris, helps lost hikers determine true north to navigate safely at night.
During a full moon, higher high tides called spring tides can unexpectedly sweep swimmers away from beaches.
During an earthquake, drop to the ground and hide under a sturdy table to protect your head from falling debris.
Drinking plenty of water and staying in the shade prevents heatstroke when playing outside on very hot days.
If you hear sudden roaring sounds or see cracking soil on a hill, run away immediately to avoid landslides.
Removing stagnant water around your house stops mosquitoes from breeding, which prevents the spread of dengue fever.
Never walk through fast-moving floodwaters because just fifteen centimeters of flowing water can easily knock you down.
